render.notes:
Rerun from scratch on 2026-10-10. The earlier run's output in sound-audition was moved to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-nathanialhenniges-Developer-mrdemonwolf-wolf-override/eb713cd4-8931-48d7-8c83-5b0b0d1e9cf3/scratchpad/sound-audition/old-run-1316 and nothing from it was reused. The repo was only read, and git status is clean. Main has moved to e54c338 (PR #43), but that change only touches apps/game/assets/changelog.txt, so sfx_bank.gd and main.gd match 975047d and the scratch copy is byte-identical to the repo's sfx_bank.gd.

Output: 69 clips, each with a PNG of the same name beside it.
- 16 from the current bank in wav/current/: 12 clips plus 4 loops tiled to 10 s.
- 53 drafts in wav/draft/:
  - footsteps: 32 variants and 8 six-step walks.
  - roomtone: 3 beds of 10 s.
  - ambient: 6 one-shots.
  - case: 4 handling sounds.

Every file is 16-bit mono 22.05 kHz with a -6.02 dBFS peak. Manifests are at wav/current/manifest.json and wav/draft/manifest.json, and measurements at analysis.json. A second render of all 53 drafts and all 16 current clips was byte-identical to the first, so the output is deterministic.

What was checked: headless rendering plus numeric and visual (PNG) checks only. Nobody has listened to any clip, nothing has been played in the game, and nothing has been tested on a device.

KEY FINDING ABOUT THE CURRENT BANK: the hum and winch loops click once per loop. At the seam the signal jumps 0.567 (hum) and 0.440 (winch), against median sample steps of 0.0055 and 0.0032. The click shows as a vertical broadband line every second in hum_loop10s.png and winch_loop10s.png. The cause is that _hum and _winch start the one-pole low-pass at low = 0, while the end of the buffer is at steady state. The sfx_bank.gd comment says "the loop seam is silent", but that only holds for the raw oscillators. A suggested fix is to run the filter for one loop length before writing samples. In game the hum plays at pitch 0.5-0.8, so the click comes about every 1.25-2 s.

The servo seam is clean. The hiss seam has no click, but its 0.5 s noise pattern repeats twice a second.

Drafts:
- Room tone beds:
  - Each bed is 5 chunks of 2 s, played from a shuffle bag with 0.25 s equal-power crossfades, plus a tonal layer on multiples of 0.5 Hz. The 10 s file also loops cleanly.
  - Seam jumps are corridor 0.0011, records 0.071 and junction 0.0079, all at or below the median sample step.
  - The 100 ms RMS around crossfades is within 0.4 dB of the RMS elsewhere.
  - Generating each bed took 356-472 ms in GDScript, against 38-40 ms for the whole current bank. Building beds at startup would blow the generation_ms budget, so they would need to be built lazily on room entry, use fewer or shorter chunks, or be split across frames.
- Footsteps:
  - All 32 variants plus the walks took about 300 ms to generate.
  - Walk step spacing comes from the stride figures in the design notes: 46 px for the engineer and 30 px for WOLF at 190 px/s, which gives 242 ms and 158 ms per step.
  - In the walk recipes, picks are 0-based: variant 0 is the file ending _1.wav.
  - I raised the wet-deck splash once from the spectrogram view so it stands apart from plate. It has not been heard.
- Low frequencies: most of the boot thump, the Junction drone's 41 Hz fundamental, distant_bang and the current boom sit below 150 Hz, which phone speakers barely reproduce. The surface cues sit above 500 Hz, so they should still read, but this needs a device listen.
- Mix levels: everything is normalised to -6 dB, as in the bank. In-game levels (beds around -20 dB, footsteps quieter than effects) still need to be set by ear.

per_clip.name: boom
per_clip.why: Truncated tail. The last sample is 0.050 and the sub is still ringing at 500 ms, so the spectrogram shows a broadband click at the end. The energy is 83% at 40-100 Hz and 7.4% below 40 Hz. Above roughly 300 Hz the clip is about 10 dB below its total RMS, so on phone and laptop speakers this boom is mostly the 0.25 s noise burst, which carries only about 10% of the energy. It is used at 0 dB for the tank hit and the door blast, so it has to read on small speakers.
per_clip.suggestion: Add a 30-50 ms fade to zero, or extend the clip to about 0.9 s so the 0.18 s tau decays fully. High-pass at 35 Hz. Drive the sub harder through tanh so 2x and 3x harmonics (90-180 Hz) imply the low end. Add a 200-600 Hz band-passed noise crunch at about -8 dB under the burst, so the hit has a body phones can play.

per_clip.name: small_boom
per_clip.why: Ends at -0.0154, a small end click. 55% of the energy is at 40-100 Hz. For a relief vent letting go, the recipe is only a pop; it has no gas-release component, and the junction already has a hiss loop it could match.
per_clip.suggestion: Fade the last 20 ms. After the pop, add a 0.3-0.5 s decaying band-passed hiss (1-4 kHz, falling) so it reads as a vent venting rather than a small explosion. High-pass at 40 Hz.

per_clip.name: clank
per_clip.why: At 40 ms the 12 ms-tau ring has fallen only to about -29 dB, and the clip ends at -0.011, a truncation click. The square ring puts 79% of the energy at 300-1000 Hz with harmonic partials, so pitched to 0.55-2.2 across about eight call sites it sounds like a buzzer blip rather than metal. It is the most reused clip in the bank.
per_clip.suggestion: Extend to 90-120 ms with a 5 ms fade. Replace the square with 3-4 inharmonic sine modes (for example 420, 1130, 2210 and 3480 Hz with decreasing tau) plus the noise tick. Consider 2-3 seeded variants with a no-repeat pick, as the footsteps use, because it fires so often.

per_clip.name: thud
per_clip.why: 99.2% of the energy is at 40-100 Hz (centroid 61 Hz), which is effectively inaudible on phone speakers and weak on laptops. The tail is truncated at 80 ms: it ends at -0.036 and the spectrogram shows a vertical click line. DC offset is 0.010 (-40 dBFS) on an 80 ms clip, an asymmetric pressure pulse. It is the 0 dB fail-beat knockdown, so the player must hear it.
per_clip.suggestion: Rebuild it as a 180->110 Hz pitch-dropping body (tau 40 ms) plus a 400-900 Hz band-passed knock (tau 15 ms) and a short 2 kHz contact tick. Make it 150 ms with a 10 ms fade. Add a one-pole DC blocker or a 40 Hz high-pass.

per_clip.name: hiss
per_clip.why: No seam click (wrap step 0.099 against a 0.111 median step), but the 0.5 s noise buffer repeats twice a second, and the 2 Hz wobble is locked to the same period, so it pulses audibly. About 50% of the energy is above 2 kHz despite the '3 kHz low-pass' (a one-pole filter is only 6 dB/oct). That is a little harsh at -8 dB when the gauge is high.
per_clip.suggestion: Build a 4-6 s buffer from 3-5 noise chunks joined with equal-power crossfades (the corridor-bed method), or stream noise from an AudioStreamGenerator. Make the wobble period non-integer against the loop. Use a 2-pole low-pass at 3 kHz to tame the 2-5 kHz band.

per_clip.name: hiss_loop10s
per_clip.why: Audition tiling confirms what the base loop shows: there is no click, but the same 0.5 s grain recurs 20 times in 10 s. The spectrogram texture repeats at the yellow seams.
per_clip.suggestion: Same fix as hiss: a longer chunked buffer, with the wobble decoupled from the loop length.

per_clip.name: hum
per_clip.why: The seam clicks once per loop: a 0.567 jump against a 0.0055 median step. The last sample is 0.4995 and the first is -0.068 because the one-pole low-pass state starts at 0. The spectrogram shows a broadband vertical line every second. Otherwise it is good: 110 and 113 Hz are whole cycles, the 3 Hz beat is seamless, and harmonics to about 500 Hz survive small speakers.
per_clip.suggestion: Pre-roll the filter: run the oscillator and filter over one full loop, discard it, then record the second pass, so the state at the end matches the start. Alternatively, generate the saws band-limited (additive harmonics up to 500 Hz) with no IIR state.

per_clip.name: hum_loop10s
per_clip.why: A click every 1 s seam, visible as ten vertical broadband lines. This would be audible throughout the junction pump scene.
per_clip.suggestion: Same filter pre-roll fix as hum.

per_clip.name: arc
per_clip.why: Very bright: 54% of the energy is above 5 kHz and the centroid is 5.4 kHz. There is almost nothing below 1 kHz (2.4%), so the arc lacks body. Crest is 20.8 dB (RMS -26.8 dBFS), so at the same peak it will play about 12-17 dB quieter in perceived loudness than klaxon or hum, while its fizz sits in the harsh band. The clip edges are clean.
per_clip.suggestion: Add a 100/120 Hz-gated buzz band-passed at 300-1500 Hz under the crackle for the first 150 ms (the 'zzt' body), and roll off the crackle above 6 kHz by a few dB. Raise the call-site gains, or normalise the bank by RMS rather than peak.

per_clip.name: klaxon
per_clip.why: The 2.5 kHz low-pass leaves 93% of the energy at the 880 Hz fundamental, so it reads as a clean microwave-timer beep rather than an industrial warning. Crest is 3.2 dB (RMS -9.2 dBFS), making it by far the loudest clip by RMS, about 17 dB above arc at the same peak, and it plays at -4 dB. The ramps are clean and there are no clicks.
per_clip.suggestion: Make it a two-tone or slightly detuned pair (for example 880 Hz plus 1046 or 660 Hz, or a 5-cent detuned second square), keep some third harmonic (raise the low-pass to about 3.5 kHz), and drop the call-site gain to about -10 dB.

per_clip.name: growl
per_clip.why: 65% of the energy is at 40-100 Hz (the 70->58 Hz saw fundamental) behind a 900 Hz low-pass, with only 7.8% at 300-1000 Hz. On phone speakers WOLF's growl will be thin and quiet, yet it is a character beat. The envelope (80 ms swell, 0.2 s die-away, ends at 0) and the 9 Hz tremolo are good.
per_clip.suggestion: Raise the low-pass to about 1.8 kHz and add a formant band-pass around 450-700 Hz (Q 2-3) on the saw, about +6 dB, so the growl's identity lives where small speakers play. Add light tanh grit for a metallic edge. Keep the sub, but high-pass at 45 Hz.

per_clip.name: servo
per_clip.why: The loop is seamless (whole cycles; the seam step equals a normal step). But 84.5% of the energy is in a single 1.2 kHz sine with vibrato, so it reads as a test-tone whistle or theremin rather than a sentry motor. A pure tone at 1.2 kHz also cuts through every speaker and can fatigue over a long sentry encounter.
per_clip.suggestion: Keep the seamless whole-cycle design, but add gear texture: a 2.4 kHz harmonic at about 0.2, a 3-5% amplitude ripple at an integer gear-tooth rate (for example 40 Hz), and a faint band-passed noise (1-3 kHz) whose envelope also loops in whole cycles. Drop the fundamental 3 dB.

per_clip.name: servo_loop10s
per_clip.why: Tiled 10 s confirms it is seamless. The only issue is timbre: the pure whistle.
per_clip.suggestion: Same harmonic and gear-ripple additions as servo, keeping whole cycles per loop.

per_clip.name: winch
per_clip.why: Clicks once per loop: a 0.440 jump against a 0.0032 median step (last 0.375, first -0.066), from the same one-pole filter state restart as hum. Timbre is OK: a 90 Hz saw with a 7 Hz wobble, 50% at 40-100 Hz and 41% at 100-300 Hz.
per_clip.suggestion: Pre-roll the filter one loop as for hum. Add a faint integer-rate (for example 14 Hz) ratchet or tick layer at 1-2 kHz so it reads as a winch on phones.

per_clip.name: winch_loop10s
per_clip.why: A click at every 1 s seam in the tiled audition.
per_clip.suggestion: Same filter pre-roll fix as winch.

per_clip.name: whine

per_clip.suggestion: Low-pass the hiss with a 2-pole filter at about 3.5 kHz plus a pink tilt, and drop it 10-12 dB against the transformer buzz so the buzz carries the room. Keep the micro-crackle sparse. Target about -32 dBFS RMS in game.

per_clip.suggestion: High-pass at 40 Hz and cut the brown rumble about 10 dB. Soft-saturate the 41 Hz drone so its 82/123/164 Hz harmonics imply the fundamental. Lift the metal partials (137/211/389/523 Hz) and the 660 Hz Q8 band 6-8 dB. Add a slow-beating pair near 260 Hz for size. Re-check with a 100 ms RMS profile.

crit.overall:
I judged all 69 clips from measurements, not by ear. A stdlib Python analyser checked RMS, crest, DC, start and end samples, the loop wrap step, head versus tail 50 ms, the band split and a 100 ms time profile for the beds. I also inspected the PNGs. Nothing is hard-clipped (0 samples at full scale), and DC is negligible everywhere except current thud (0.010) and a small offset in the footsteps and the Junction bed (about 0.002-0.004).

Five recurring problems:

1. **Small speakers.** The bank leans heavily on sub-100 Hz content that phone and laptop speakers cannot play. Affected clips: thud (99% at 40-100 Hz), boom (90% below 100 Hz), growl, distant_bang, junction_bed (35% below 40 Hz), and the engineer plate, wet and rubble steps, which are over 80% below 300 Hz with a 300-1000 Hz hole. The fix in each recipe is to high-pass at 35-50 Hz, saturate the lows so their harmonics imply the fundamental, and add a 200-1000 Hz body layer. Thud needs a full redo because its fail-beat role must be audible.

2. **Loop seams.** hum and winch click every loop because the one-pole low-pass state restarts at 0 (jumps of 0.567 and 0.440). Pre-rolling the filter for one loop fixes both. The 0.5 s hiss is click-free but audibly repeats twice a second, so it should use the chunked crossfade method the drafts already use. servo and all three draft beds are seamless.

3. **Truncated tails.** boom, small_boom, clank and thud end on non-zero samples, which shows as end clicks in the spectrograms. They need 10-50 ms fades. All the draft one-shots start and end at exactly 0, which is good.

4. **Peak normalisation.** Normalising everything to -6 dBFS peak gives a 17 dB RMS spread: klaxon is at -9 dBFS RMS, while arc and the ticks are at -27 to -30. Either normalise by RMS or short-term loudness, or compensate at the call sites. The klaxon, a near-pure 880 Hz beep at -4 dB, will be the loudest thing in the game.

5. **Variety and beds.** WOLF's plate paws use identical claw and pad partials in every variant, so the walk spectrogram shows six identical stacks and only the pitch jitter separates them; the frequencies should be randomised per variant. The wolf_rubble variants need gain-matching (3.2 dB spread). Among the beds, corridor is ready. Records is a bright 4.5 kHz-centroid fizz rather than a hush and needs a low-pass with the hiss dropped under the transformer buzz. Junction needs its rumble swapped for audible metal partials.

The grating steps for both characters, all WOLF wet and rubble steps, the evidence-case set (rustle, clack, clink, ratchet), drip, pipe_creak, cooling_tick, vent_flutter and whine are keep. The walk renders confirm the no-repeat pick and the +/-6% pitch and +/-2 dB jitter behave: per-step peaks spread about 2-3 dB.

None of this has been listened to, so any keep is provisional until someone hears the clips on a laptop and a phone. The measurement scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-nathanialhenniges-Developer-mrdemonwolf-wolf-override/eb713cd4-8931-48d7-8c83-5b0b0d1e9cf3/scratchpad/critic (an.py, with results in m.json). The repository was not touched.
